title: Networking 2
description: Ops pages VDI: websites will not load. Public and internal nslookup is failing. Applications that need to reach back on-prem are disrupted.
scope: Out-of-hours: sites failing to load, public and internal DNS lookups failing, on-prem applications disrupted.
illustrativeDisclaimer: This scenario, its mock incident, runbook titles, product names, escalation routes, and organisational procedures are illustrative. Validate them against approved operational sources before use. They are not bank-specific policy.
assessorGuidance: Reward two DNS planes, not ‘the desktop is down’. nslookup public and internal. PAA handles DNS for basically all of its traffic. Infoblox on-prem serves DNS for native-NIC traffic that PAA does not manage. Compare AVD with corp physical (Modern Workplace can help). Ops, TRM if not on. If the failing lookups sit on PAA, engage proxy / Palo via the official path. If they sit on native NIC, Infoblox / DNS owners. Safety-critical: do not say it is AVD until proven, and do not change PAA DNS or Infoblox yourself with no INC and no CR.
acceptableAlternativeApproaches: nslookup public and internal first, then split PAA DNS versus Infoblox native NIC, then the owning team.
Physical device with MW first to show it is not AVD-only, then the two DNS planes.
Ops and TRM on while VDI packs which plane failed and who owns it.

questions.prompt: Walk through how you would handle this incident from the first call through to recovery. Write the full response in your own words.
questions.helpText: Name resolution is failing. Think about how DNS is handled on this platform — not all traffic uses the same resolvers.
questions.assessorGuidance: Score the whole write-up. Reward: public and internal nslookup; PAA DNS versus Infoblox native NIC; AVD versus physical (MW can help); Ops and TRM; proxy/Palo if PAA path, Infoblox owners if native NIC; recovery when lookups and users on the call work. Do not score as demonstrated: ‘AVD is down’ because sites fail from the desktop; changing PAA DNS or Infoblox with no INC/CR; checking only one DNS plane.

scoringCriteria.label: Treats this as name resolution (sites and on-prem reach-back), not as ‘AVD will not connect’
Runs public and internal nslookup and splits PAA DNS from Infoblox on the native NIC
Uses the fact that PAA handles DNS for basically all of its traffic, and engages proxy / Palo when that plane is failing
Gets Ops (and TRM if needed) to bring Infoblox / DNS owners on the native-NIC plane, and vendors only for the plane that is actually failing
Brings TRM in if they are not already engaged on a wide DNS disruption
Proves recovery with working public and internal lookups and users on the call loading sites / reaching on-prem apps
Does not call it AVD until proven, and does not change PAA DNS or Infoblox without INC and CR
